summary: Scheduled service account token refresh failing after Okta policy update — nightly model-evals jobs stopped
description:
Issue summary:
- On 2026-02-28 ~01:10 UTC, multiple nightly model-evals cron jobs (model-eval-pipeline) failed to start; investigation shows the service account refresh token used by the scheduler returned invalid_grant.

Impact:
- Nightly evaluation and validation runs did not complete for ~6 hours (primary impact: model quality dashboards stale; secondary: delayed nightly cost reports).
- Approximately 12 scheduled jobs in prod us-east failed and retried until exhaustion.

Environment:
- Production cluster (k8s), us-east region.
- Scheduler: kubernetes CronJob invoking eval-runner service which requests a refreshed access token from identity-broker via Okta refresh token flow.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) CronJob triggers eval-runner pod.
2) Eval-runner calls identity-broker /oauth2/token with grant_type=refresh_token and service-account refresh token.
3) Identity-broker calls Okta token endpoint; Okta responds 400 invalid_grant and revokes refresh token.
4) Eval-runner fails and exits; scheduler marks job failed.

Observed behavior:
- Okta token endpoint returns HTTP 400 with body: {"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"The refresh token is invalid or has been revoked"}.
- No prior token rotation event recorded in platform key-rotation logs.

Expected behavior:
- Service account refresh tokens used by scheduled jobs should remain valid for rotation window or be automatically rotated by our token broker without causing job failures.

Initial hypothesis:
- A recent Okta Conditional Access policy enforcement (device trust) was tightened and inadvertently targeted the OU or client used by service account tokens, triggering revocation of refresh tokens for non-interactive sessions.

Telemetry and logs (excerpt):
- identity-broker logs (2026-02-28T01:09:58Z): "refresh token exchange failed: invalid_grant, okta error: token revoked by policy"
- scheduler logs (job eval-20260228-01): "Failed to obtain access token, retry count 0, aborting"
- Okta audit (admin): policy change id=pol-2026-02-27-7 by admin.carol -> enforced device_trust=true for group '/Services/NonInteractive'
comments: 2026-02-28 02:18 - Support Intake (Aisha): Initial ticket created after alerting on 12 failed cron runs. Notified #infra-ops and #platform-auth.
2026-02-28 03:05 - Marco H.: Started triage. Confirmed identity-broker received 400 invalid_grant from Okta. Pulling Okta audit logs next.
2026-02-28 03:40 - Lina S. (SRE): Observed the same pattern on two other non-eval cronjobs (backup-prune, billing-usage). Possibly broad impact to non-interactive service accounts.

2026-02-28 04:05 - Marco H.: Found Okta admin change: policy pol-2026-02-27-7 enabled device_trust and applied to group '/Services/NonInteractive' at 2026-02-27T23:57Z. Reached out to Identity team to request rollback or exception.

2026-02-28 05:20 - Identity Team (J. O'Neil): Confirmed policy rollout targeted the wrong group due to matching rule. We are reverting the policy to prior state and will create an allowlist for machine identities. Revert scheduled at 05:45 UTC.
2026-02-28 06:00 - Marco H.: Revert applied. Running a full retry of queued cron jobs. 10/12 jobs completed successfully after revert; 2 require manual rerun due to retry exhaustion—requeued.

2026-03-01 09:30 - Platform Eng (R. Gupta): Proposing permanent mitigation: migrate cron jobs to use Client Credentials flow (OAuth2.0) with rotation via Vault-issued JWTs and remove dependency on long-lived refresh tokens tied to interactive Okta policies.
2026-03-02 14:12 - Marco H.: Implemented emergency workaround doc and scheduled follow-up epic to migrate eval-runner to new token-broker flow. Assigned owners and timeline in linked Confluence.
2026-03-02 16:00 - Aisha P.: Customer-facing alert not required (internal-only). Closing impact window. Keeping ticket open until migration is complete.
investigation_notes: Okta audit proves root cause: policy pol-2026-02-27-7 incorrectly matched '/Services/NonInteractive' and revoked refresh tokens for that group.

identity-broker treats Okta invalid_grant as non-retriable and fails job; this is expected but we should handle targeted policy revocations more gracefully (circuit-breaker + alerting to identity team).
Token rotation metadata shows last successful rotation for service-account 'svc-eval-runner' at 2026-02-20; no scheduled rotation in last week. Revocation was external (policy), not expired token.
We observed collateral failures in backup-prune and billing-usage cronjobs confirming policy scope was broad.
logs: [identity-broker][2026-02-28T01:09:58Z] ERROR token_exchange.go:124 - refresh exchange failed for svc-eval-runner: okta response 400 invalid_grant (token revoked by policy)
[okta-audit][2026-02-27T23:57:12Z] ADMIN admin.carol - updated policy pol-2026-02-27-7 target: /Services/NonInteractive - device_trust=true
[scheduler][2026-02-28T01:10:03Z] cronjob eval-20260228-01 failed: unable to authenticate: refresh failed
workaround: Identity team reverted the policy at 2026-02-28T05:45 UTC which restored token refresh for affected service accounts. Two jobs that exhausted retries were manually requeued and completed. Temporary exception created for '/Services/NonInteractive' until permanent fix is live.
resolution_notes:
Short-term: Policy revert and allowlist for machine identities applied (completed).
Mid-term: Implement client-credentials-based broker for cron jobs and migrate eval-runner and other cron consumers.
Long-term: Add automated pre-deploy policy impact check and alerting when a policy targets groups with service-account clients. Add test coverage for non-interactive OU matching.
Owners: Identity team (lead J. O'Neil) for policy rules; Platform Eng (R. Gupta) for token migration; SRE (Lina S.) for runbook updates.
